column1: # status is DECLARED, never inferred from the outcome:
#   supported  the feature is built; a failure here FAILS the run
#   planned    the feature is not built; an expected failure, reported as
#              PLANNED and not counted against the run
#   n/a        Go semantics bash++ explicitly does not claim
# Declaring status is what lets a TDD suite be honest. Inferring it from the
# result would mean a regression in a shipped feature could quietly re-label
# itself as "not built yet" — the suite would go green by forgetting.
# The script itself passes under plain --posix; it fails only because the
# --bashpp SELECTOR does not exist yet (P0 activation, story B1). So the
# unbuilt feature is activation, not this fixture, and every fixture in the
# suite is blocked behind the same flag. That is worth seeing in the report.
